critical: aria-allowed-attr: 1 node on every page in this flow (homepage, category page, general listing, filtered listing) — some element carries an ARIA attribute not valid for its role. Not previously seen in the admin-panel's category-management scan; this is a storefront-specific finding.
serious: aria-prohibited-attr: up to 12 nodes on the homepage and general listing — related to the aria-allowed-attr finding above, likely the same underlying component(s) since both fired together on the same pages.
color-contrast: 4-10 nodes on the homepage and listing pages.
moderate: document-title: 1 node on the category page (Business Cards) — axe flagged a missing/empty document title at scan time, despite generateMetadata setting title: category.name in source; possibly a timing artifact of when axe sampled relative to the client-side title update, not necessarily a real gap. Worth a manual check rather than assuming either way.

page-has-heading-one: 1 node on the category page — same page as the document-title finding above; the plan's own hp-03 step confirmed an <h1> with the category name IS present and visible at that point in the flow, so this is likely the same sampling-timing question, not a contradiction to take at face value.
accessibility_summary.coverage_caveat: automated scan only — manual/screen-reader review still needed

concerns: Lighthouse was deliberately left off for every run in this suite to keep CPU usage down on a resource-constrained environment — no performance numbers were collected.

ux_gaps.issue: A React hydration mismatch (server/client-mismatched attributes, 'won't be patched up') is logged as a console error on both the homepage and the general product listing. This is structurally the same class of warning independently found on the admin panel's login page (see category-management-analysis.json) — two separate Next.js codebases showing the same warning shape raises the odds this is environment/headless-browser noise (the warning's own text names a browser extension as one possible cause) rather than two coincidentally-identical app bugs, but that's a hypothesis, not a conclusion.

recommendations.action: Investigate the aria-allowed-attr (critical) and aria-prohibited-attr (serious) violations recurring across every storefront page in this flow — a shared component is the likely single source given how consistently they co-occur.
Audit the shared color-contrast tokens (likely overlaps with the same audit recommended for the admin panel).

Manually verify the document-title / page-has-heading-one findings on the category page in a real browser — the plan's own live-run evidence (a visible, correct <h1>) suggests these may be axe-sampling-timing artifacts rather than real gaps, but that needs eyes-on confirmation, not an assumption either way.
Manually verify the hydration-mismatch console warning on a real browser (both here and on the admin panel's login page) before assuming it's test-environment noise.
